author: Shareholders Unite
title: We had bought shares of Lumentum ( LITE ) for the SHU portfo
text:
We had bought shares of Lumentum ( LITE ) for the SHU portfolio in a previous decline at $45, but the bad news from Apple's ( AAPL ) new iPhone X started to sully the share price again and we became a little wary.
Was that 3D sensing and face recognition all a fad? Were other mobiles actually going to incorporate it? We were starting to have some doubts, we admit.
Some of these doubts seem actually to be vindicated when Lumentum produced the Q2 results, which indicated a stellar December quarter but the guidance for their March (and June) quarters was below par.
This looked exactly like the Apple faithful bought the iPhone X in droves just when it came out, but demand is really tapering off, just as many rumor reports predicted. There were even reports that argued the iPhone X would be discontinued prematurely. On the other hand, there were some counterarguments as well, from MarketWatch :
Apple shares declined Monday after a report that iPhone production had slowed. If that sounds familiar, congratulations for paying attention. The big difference this time is that the production-decline rumors are coming a month later than normal for the iPhone X, which should be expected because that new model began selling later than other iPhones. The Nikkei Asian Review wrote Monday that Apple AAPL, -1.26% will produce half as many iPhone X units as it initially expected during the March quarter, and analysts at JP Morgan commented last week that the company halved its build orders for the March period relative to the holiday quarter. Apple investors should be familiar with this show. iPhone shipments traditionally peak during the holiday quarter, right after a new model is announced. Then they taper off in the new year as shoppers opt for a greater mix of older models—or figure they can wait around until the next latest and greatest version comes out in the fall.
